conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: the claim is true, not false (in the U.S.).** Kyleena is FDA-approved/labelled for prevention of pregnancy for **up to five years**. The FDA-approved prescribing-information label states: “Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years” and directs that it be replaced after five years if continued use is desired.

The five-year duration is supported by clinical-trial contraceptive outcomes in the product information. The reported first-year Pearl Index was 0.16 (a low pregnancy rate), and the estimated cumulative pregnancy rate across five years was 1.45% (13 pregnancies), with a 95% upper confidence limit of 2.53%. This does not mean pregnancy is impossible; it means the device has demonstrated contraceptive effectiveness through its labeled five-year use period.

A possible source of confusion is that “approved for up to five years” is a regulatory indication and replacement limit, not a guarantee of zero pregnancies or a statement that every individual device remains equally effective beyond five years. The current label says replacement is needed after five years for ongoing contraception.

Sources:  
- https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2023/208224s005lbl.pdf  
- https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080  
- https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy
